newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Two key parties worry about Westpac bid.
newsitem.headline: Two key parties worry about Westpac bid.

text.p: Australia's major non-government parties, the Labor and Democrat parties, both expressed concern on Thursday at the proposed takeover of Bank of Melbourne Ltd by the much larger Westpac Banking Corp.

The Democrats and Labor said consumers would be the losers if the government supported bank mergers as part of its recommendations from the Wallis inquiry into financial institutions, due to be released on or after April 7.

The merger, announced on Thursday, is subject to approval from the national monopolies watchdog, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission, and from the Liberal-National government's treasurer, Peter Costello.
Democrats Leader Cheryl Kernot said the proposal prompted her concern that bank mergers would reduce competition and increase the opportunities for the big banks to fix prices.
"If the takeover succeeds, the big four banks will control 87 percent of the Victorian (state) banking market," Kernot said in a statement.

"And if the Wallis inquiry comes up with recommendations the government appears to want and one of the 'big four' banks swallows another, that will leave three banks with 87 percent of the market," Kernot said.
The big four are Westpac, National Australia Bank Ltd, Commonwealth Bank of Australia and Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd.
Labor Treasury spokesman Gareth Evans said he was concerned about job losses, rural services, competition and the implications for retail bank customers.
The Wallis inquiry, headed by prominent businessman Stan Wallis, is the first major review of the Australian finance sector regulations since the early 1980s.
It is expected to include a recommendation to end the current "six pillars" policy which prevents mergers between the four big Australian banks and the two largest life offices.
The government does not control the Senate, the upper house of parliament. But Labor and Democrat legislative backing is not needed if the deal is approved under current laws.
